g.text: Anatomy of an NVL72 rack (schematic, typical GB200/GB300 layout)
① FRONT VIEW - what fills the rack (top to bottom)
② REAR - the four hidden systems that make 72 GPUs one machine

text.tspan: ~120 kW IT (~145 kW incl. network share)
20.7 TB HBM4 + 54 TB LPDDR5X · cable-free trays

g.text: Out-of-band management switch (BMC network to every tray)

text.tspan: 1U each · 6 × 5.5 kW PSUs = up to 33 kW · AC in → ~50 V DC out
each = 2 Grace CPUs + 4 Blackwell GPUs (two superchips)
+ SuperNICs, DPU, NVMe · cold plates on every CPU and GPU
2 NVLink switch chips per tray = 18 per rack (Vera Rubin: 36)
144 NVLink ports per tray · no CPU, no GPU
8 shelves in NVIDIA's DGX configuration (OEM layouts vary)
~5,000 copper cables, ~2 miles, in blind-mate cable cartridges
every GPU reaches all 72 at 1.8 TB/s (NVLink 5) → ~130 TB/s all-to-all
copper instead of optics saves ~20 kW of transceivers per rack
vertical copper bar carries ~50 V DC from the power shelves to every tray
~132 kW at ~50 V is ~2,600 A - why NVIDIA wants 800 V DC for 2027 racks
supply + return pipes with quick-disconnects to every compute and switch tray
cold plates take most of the heat; fans clear the residue (Vera Rubin: fanless trays)
SuperNIC ports leave the rack to leaf switches in separate network racks
(800 Gb/s per GPU on GB300; 1.6 Tb/s per GPU on Vera Rubin)
in-row or in-rack: pumps the rack's coolant loop and
hands heat to facility water through a heat exchanger
